messages:
Maya Patel: quick check before merge — small change to text-gen routing. Client payload: {"model_id":"redwood-3b-v2","routing_hints":{"region":"eu-west-1","tier":"standard"}}. What's fallback order and what do we promise back about which model served it?
Jonah: current plan: (1) exact model in requested region+tier, (2) same-family equivalent in region+tier, (3) quantized/compatible variant in region, (4) cross-region fallback by policy, (5) smaller capacity model if customer allows. docs scattered.
kevin: pin_model=true must not silently substitute. some private deploys returned 422. Propose 409 and structured error.
Sofia: agree 409. Error body suggestion: {"error":"ModelPinnedUnavailable","detail":"Requested model is pinned but not available in eu-west-1"}.
Maya Patel: for non-pinned, want a way to log which model answered. Proposal: add served_model string in response body, e.g. {"id":...,"choices":...,"served_model":"redwood-3b-v2-quant"}.
Jonah: body field could break strict schemas. Gate behind Prefer header for rollout.
kevin: header x-served-model is safer and less invasive, but proxies may strip headers.
Sofia: do both. Emit x-served-model header always, and only include served_model in body when client sends Prefer: include-served-model=true for initial rollout. Also consider x-served-tier if tier differs.
Maya Patel: agreed. Implement: x-served-model header always, body served_model only when Prefer present. Gate for 2 weeks then flip default.
Jonah: region_hint vs tier mismatch: options: strict (error), soft (try match and report served_tier), permissive (ignore). I prefer soft default, allow strict_tier=true to force 409.
kevin: soft default with strict opt-in for enterprise customers. strict_tier true => 409 if incompatible.
Maya Patel: PR checklist: add header, body field gated by Prefer, support strict_tier boolean, update API docs, add e2e asserting header+body match.
Sofia: I'll own docs and release notes. QA Sara will run SDK smoke tests.
QA Sara: test matrix: a) exact model available -> header + body (when prefer) match; b) family fallback -> served_model points to variant; c) pin + unavailable -> 409 with ModelPinnedUnavailable; d) strict_tier true + incompatible -> 409; e) Prefer header controls presence of body field.
kevin: adding unit tests and a linter to prevent body served_model without header. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/12567 assigned to @Maya_Patel and @Jonah.
Maya Patel: left naming comments (served_model vs served_model_id), prefer single string id, no nested metadata for now.
infra-bot: Canary started: served-model-rollout -> 10% traffic -> eu-west-1.
QA Sara: e2e on canary discovered a client with strict json-schemas crashed when served_model appeared even without Prefer header. investigating proxy mutation.
Jonah: roll canary back to 0% while we debug body leak.
infra-bot: Canary rolled back to 0%: served-model-rollout.
Maya Patel: action plan: (1) revert body-field change from canary, (2) keep x-served-model header only, (3) publish docs and migration notes, (4) reintroduce body field behind Prefer after docs/comms.
Sofia: adding docs tasks to api-contracts sprint and notifying SDK owners.
kevin: updating PR and tests. will contact top SDK owners. :thumbsup: 
Maya Patel: filing short RFC for final contract and timeline. Tagging follow-ups: @QA_Sara to validate SDKs, @Sofia to publish docs, @kevin to update PR.
Sofia: agreed, closing loop after docs + 1-week verification window.
